newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-selling.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Monday on short-selling at higher levels, triggered by losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday, traders said.
Trading became more active with the battle between short-covering and short-selling lasting most of the session, they said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 22,720 yuan ($2,739) per tonne, losing 190 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 22,650 and hit a high of 22,770 yuan per tonne.
April fell 110 yuan to 23,020, May 160 to 22,890, June 100 to 22,860, August 160 to 22,730 and September 170 to 22,700.
Combined volume rose sharply to 52,730 tonnes from 25,910.
Copper opened lower and short-covering pushed prices from their lows but were again pressed down by short-selling to end lower, traders said.

Traders said the outlook for market direction was in favour of the shorts. Contracts maturing after July are mainly held by institutional sellers who could more easily control this market that sellers, they said.
Traders suggested a "hold" in short positions and perhaps a building of positions at suitable lower prices for quick profits.
Prices for physical copper are around 23,200 to 23,300 yuan per tonne, down from 23,400 yuan last week, they said.
Aluminium ended down across the board. April fell 100 to 15,400 yuan per tonne, May 120 yuan to 15,480 and June 100 to 15,650 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 1,140 tonnes from 780 tonnes.
